title: GPU IAM least-privilege onboarding and IaC assertions
author: Arjun Patel
body:
Summary

This page documents the recommended least-privilege IAM patterns for GPU tenant onboarding and the corresponding Terraform / IaC assertions we run as part of the provisioning pipeline. It is intended for infra engineers responsible for tenant onboarding, module authors, and security reviewers.

Goals
- Ensure GPU tenancy, egress, and billing service accounts are provisioned with minimal privileges required for runtime and observability.
- Encode assertions in IaC so misconfigurations are detected during CI (fail fast).
- Provide reusable policy snippets and examples that map to common GPU fleet services (scheduler, warm-pool, spot-drainer, billing exporter).

Scope
- Applies to AWS and GCP tenant accounts that will run Redwood-managed GPU workloads.
- Covers service accounts and IAM roles used by: kube-scheduler adapter, spot-drainer, warm-pool controllers, telemetry exporters, and node bootstrap agents.
- Does not cover developer user IAM (developers use central identity provider).

Principles
1) Rule of least privilege: no service account should have permissions outside an explicit list.
2) IaC-first: all role / policy changes must be expressed in Terraform modules and covered by automated assertions.
3) Auditability: every role must include a numeric tag and owner metadata; policies must be tracked in the policy catalog.
4) Fail-fast in CI: policy linting + automated policy simulation must run for each PR that touches modules.

Roles and ownership
- infra-security: final approver for policy exceptions.
- infra-platform: module authors, responsible for delivering templates and test harnesses.
- oncall-infra: emergency remediation owner for misprovisioned permissions in prod accounts.
- customer-onboarding: executes tenant onboarding and populates owner tags.

Common service account patterns
- scheduler-sa (short-lived token rotation): privileges: read-only access to instance metadata, list/describe instances, tag management for scheduling operations.
- warmpool-controller-sa: privileges: describe/modify autoscaling groups (AWS) / instance group managers (GCP) limited to tenant-owned resource prefixes, CloudWatch/Stackdriver metrics write.
- spot-drainer-sa: privileges: describe and cordon/evict nodes, create maintenance events, write to a dedicated ops SNS/pubsub topic.
- telemetry-exporter-sa: write-only to metrics ingestion (putMetricData / custom metric write) and read-only to tagging API for resource attribution.

Example IAM policy snippets (AWS)
Note: These are minimal examples meant to be adapted. Replace ${tenant_prefix} and ${region} before use.

-- scheduler-policy.json --
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["ec2:DescribeInstances", "ec2:DescribeInstanceStatus", "ec2:CreateTags", "ec2:DeleteTags"],
      "Resource": "*",
      "Condition": {
        "StringLike": {"ec2:ResourceTag/Tenant": "${tenant_prefix}*"}
      }
    }
  ]
}

-- warmpool-policy.json --
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["autoscaling:DescribeAutoScalingGroups", "autoscaling:UpdateAutoScalingGroup"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:autoscaling:${region}:${account}:autoScalingGroup:*:autoScalingGroupName/${tenant_prefix}*"
    },
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["cloudwatch:PutMetricData"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}

Terraform integration patterns
1) Central policy catalog: a single Terraform module (infra-iam/policy-catalog) stores JSON policy documents under versioned folders. Module outputs: policy_arn, policy_version_id.
2) Tenant binding module (tenant-onboarding/iam-bindings): takes a list of roles and service account names and attaches policies via aws_iam_role_policy_attachment / google_project_iam_binding resources.
3) Assertion module (iac-assertions/policy-check): runs two checks at plan-time and CI-time:
   - policy-diff check: verifies that newly added actions are explicitly reviewed (requires a PR label and two approvers).
   - simulated-access check: invokes the cloud provider policy simulator (aws: iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy / gcp: testIamPermissions equivalent) against representative APIs used by the service.

Sample Terraform variable schema (text table)
- tenant_prefix: string (required) -- short identifier used in resource names and tags
- region: string (required) -- region where runtime resources are provisioned
- allowed_actions: list(string) (optional) -- explicit allow-list additions for corner cases
- owner_tag: string (required) -- person/team responsible for the role

CI Gates and checks (required in repo pipeline)
1) terraform fmt + validate for all modules.
2) policy-lint: run custom linter that detects wildcard actions, overly-broad Resource entries, and missing tag/owner metadata.
3) simulate-policy: run policy simulation against a small set of actions defined per role; failure = pipeline fail.
4) manual-approval: PRs that increase privileges require the label "iam-privilege-increase" and two approvers from infra-security.

Operational runbook: investigating unexpected permission escalations
1) Trigger: PagerDuty alert OR audit log detection rule firing for unexpected CreateRole/PutRolePolicy calls.
2) Triage steps:
   a) Identify affected account and role name via CloudTrail/Stackdriver logs.
   b) Check IaC repo PR history: did a recent merge touch infra-iam modules?
   c) If change exists in git: create a revert PR and notify infra-security + oncall.
   d) If change is not in git: revoke temporary credentials, detach offending policies, and create a forensic snapshot (CloudTrail export).
3) Post-mortem: required when an inline policy or wildcard privilege was granted to a prod role. Include timeline, root cause, corrective IaC change, and rollout plan.

Policy exceptions and risk acceptance
- Exceptions are permitted only with documented mitigations and a maximum 90-day window. Process: submit a Policy Exception request (label: iam-exception) with justification, alternative mitigations, and an owner. infra-security must approve.

Appendix: policy simulation matrix (example)
- scheduler-sa: simulate actions: [ec2:DescribeInstances, ec2:CreateTags] -> expected: Allow
- warmpool-controller-sa: simulate actions: [autoscaling:UpdateAutoScalingGroup] -> expected: Allow on tenant resources, Deny on other prefixes
- spot-drainer-sa: simulate actions: [eks:DescribeNodegroup, eks:UpdateNodegroupConfig] -> expected: Allow only for tenant nodegroups
